items.title: What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question
items.summary: Arguably the most realistic Grand Theft Auto game is about to come out, but there was a time when that was the last thing you could expect from the series, a cl
items.content:
"We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us."

Image credit: Transhuman Design, Skystone Games, Eurogamer. Feature by Sherif Saed Senior Contributor Published on Nov. 21, 2026, 10 a.m. 4 comments Follow Grand Theft Auto 2 Prioritise us on Google What would you get if you combined the chaotic top-down action of old-school Grand Theft Auto 2 with the chaotic top-down action of Vampire Survivors? That's the question Soldat and King Arthur's Gold developer Transhuman asked when it started working on 2024's roguelite shooter Maniac. The result is a delight, yet Maniac remains frustratingly underappreciated.

Your goal is simple: survive for as long as you can or until the 20-minute clock hits zero. Throughout that time, your secondary objective is to create as much mayhem as possible - painting the road with the blood of your foes, slamming cars into buildings, performing drive-bys as you rampage across the procedurally-generated city. The more carnage you cause, the higher your Wanted level, until you're fending off police and the military.

Maniac's debt to GTA is clear, and its chaotic action is brilliantly realised as it channels the compelling rhythms of a Survivors-style roguelite, where randomness in items and level layout makes each run fresh as you strive to unlock new characters, progressing a little further each time. It's a relatively slight experience, as its £4 price tag reflects, featuring a single compact map, just six characters, and barely any permanent progression. But Maniac makes a spirited argument for a return to a simpler time when GTA was all about shooting cops, stealing cars, and indiscriminately murdering pedestrians rather than the 'everything' game it is today.

Maniac is also a game that feels like it's trying to make good on an idea many of us had when we first played GTA 1 & 2 all those years ago: what would a better-looking, more advanced version of that look like? And for developer Michał Marcinkowski, Maniac's genesis also harkens back to an earlier time. "When I was 12, I used to come back from school and play the demo of GTA 1," he tells me over email. "It was top-down and time-limited, and all I'd do was try to cause as much chaos as possible within the 20 minutes of the demo."

And there's perhaps a hint of a 12-year-old's exuberance to Maniac. There's the bright colour palette and gleeful chaos of its physics-driven mechanics, the adrenaline rush its aggressive enemy AI creates, and its absurd roster of playable characters, which range from Little Girl to Hotdog Guy. "Each [character] is a bit of me and a bit of you," Marcinkowski explains. "We all have a drunk Santa in us. We all have a pathetic hot-dog-suit guy inside of us. Each character failed at something and is lashing out."

As each new Grand Theft Auto game pushes further into realism, the idea of recreating the rampages seen in classic GTA feels increasingly unpalatable, but Maniac's colourful cartoon aesthetic means it can get away with more. One Achievement, with a flourish of old-school bad-taste humour, challenges players to destroy five school buses using an airstrike ability called Santa's Little Helpers. And that level of irreverent, chaotic lunacy escalates the deeper into each session you get, particularly as your Wanted level climbs: if you antagonise law enforcement enough here, they eventually break out a game-ending nuke.

"This comes back to being 12," Marcinkowski says. "Nukes are just cool. I wanted the game to end with a bang, and what's more maniacal and exaggerated than a nuke? So that idea was with me for more than 20 years."

Core to Maniac's design is the ability to change from a Survivors-like auto-shooter to a standard shooter where you're able to control your aim. The latter option is, I think, the more fitting one, particularly given how much driving you do. If you squint, it almost feels like a GTA 2 clone. And while the Vampire Survivors inspirations are plentiful - including its now-standard three-option upgrade system - the GTA elements are clearly the more prevalent.

It might not play exactly like a GTA game, but it certainly captures the series' early days spirit. And Marcinkowski says he's surprised more developers haven't tried to riff on GTA: "You'd expect the most popular game in the world to have hundreds of clones, but that's not the case." There may be a reason for that.

As big as modern-day GTA is, clones are apparently much less popular. "When you look at the sales data, particularly of top-down GTA clones, they don't sell well", explains Marcinkowski. "I found that out way too late, and I thought Maniac wouldn't be a hit." His publisher was initially equally buoyant too. "But then they studied the market and stopped being so hyped. That's how it felt as we got close to release. The wishlist count wasn't very high."

"I was expecting 10,000 [copies sold]," Marcinkowski tells me. "I actually started making another game two months before Maniac came out because I thought I'd go broke." But then the game launched, and early worries proved unfounded. It sold more than 100K copies, comfortably blowing past its maker's modest expectations, putting it in the top one percent of games released on Steam.

It's a surprise success story built on the foundations of Marcinkowski's youth, and as we chat about GTA, he reveals he's less keen on Rockstar's modern games, which lack that classic gameplay drive. "I always liked the counter-culture side of GTA, which is why I put so much of it into Maniac," he elaborates. " GTA 6 seems to have become pop culture, so it's lost its appeal for me." Marcinkowski's heart, it seems, is old-school.

items.title: Warhammer Survivors Review: Damn Good Fun!
items.summary: Warhammer Survivors combines Vampire Survivors action with 40K and Age of Sigmar. Is Auroch Digital's addictive roguelite worth playing? Find out.
items.content:
If you like Vampire Survivors and Warhammer then Warhammer Survivors is definitely your thing. Auroch Digital have taken a very addictive gameplay formula, loaded it with a massive array of Warhammer characters, weapons and enemies and come up with something that is absolutely great fun. It doesn’t need to reinvent the wheel really. Sometimes you just want to jump in, kill off the ludicrous number of enemies and watch your character become an ever more deadly walking arsenal of destruction. Warhammer Survivors does exactly that.

Developed and published by Auroch Digital (creators of Warhammer 40k: Boltgun) in conjunction with Vampire Survivors’ creator poncle, this is an officially licensed bullet heaven roguelite which brings together the two very different sides of the Warhammer universe (Warhammer 40k and Warhammer Age of Sigmar). You’ve got the champions, the enemies, the environments and the weapons of both universes all getting the pixel art treatment.

It’s a perfect combination really. Vampire Survivors has that absolutely addictive ‘one more run’ quality which very quickly becomes several more runs. Warhammer on the other hand has decades of characters, factions and utterly ridiculous weapons to choose from. Combine the two and you’ve got a huge amount of potential for anarchy.

The basic gameplay is of course very much in the Vampire Survivors mould. You pick a character, go into a stage and just try to survive the increasingly hostile waves of enemies. Your attacks are pretty much entirely automated so you’re left to focus on movement, positioning and picking up the experience to level up your character.

As you level up you can pick up new weapons, improve the ones you already have and acquire passive abilities that work in conjunction with your build. The idea is to create ever more potent combinations that can deal with the increasing numbers of enemies on screen. If you survive long enough you’ll come up against some genuinely nasty bosses and each stage is essentially a 25 minute survival run.

It’s a simple concept really, that’s what makes it so effective. There’s always another upgrade to chase, another weapon combo to try, another character to unlock. One run might go tits up but that doesn’t necessarily mean you’ve wasted your time. The gold and completed objectives all go towards unlocking more content and improving your next go.

The Warhammer setting gives this well-worn formula its own personality. It doesn’t just swap the monsters out for Space Marines and call it a day. Auroch Digital have actually brought in two very different universes, each with their own set of characters, enemies, stages and objectives.

Warhammer 40,00Warhammer 40k fans can go in and face the terrors of the 41st Millennium, Age of Sigmar brings its own range of heroes and villains from the Mortal Realms. There’s a real variety of content available, particularly if you’re a fan of both franchises.champions and a ridiculous arsenal

One of the big draws is the playable roster. There’s over 40 characters in Warhammer Survivors taken from both Warhammer 40k and Age of Sigmar. Each has their own starting weapon and stats so you can go about a run in a variety of ways.

There are some real gems for fans of the franchise in the form of Commissar Sebastian Yarrick, Stormcast Eternal Neave Blacktalon and Malum Caedo from Warhammer 40k: Boltgun. A big part of the fun is having characters from all over the Warhammer universe in one place, which is why you have such a wide variety of reasons to keep playing.

Weapon selection is just as good fun with over 75 weapons on offer. Of course you’ve got the usual Warhammer fare in there (Bolters, Chainswords, Whirlwind Axes etc) but Auroch Digital have also managed to fit in a fair number of the more unusual as well.

Anyone who’s ever been in the hobby side of Warhammer will know about the inclusion of things like Nuln Oil along with all the other painting and modelling references. It’s a great bit of cheek, particularly when you take something as mundane as a pot of miniature paint and turn it into a weapon of mass destruction.

Weapons can also be combined with passive upgrades to unlock more powerful evolved forms. Working towards these combinations is an important part of the experience, as finding the right equipment and improvements can completely change how effective your character becomes.

There’s a satisfying amount of experimentation involved, and unlocking additional weapons through character challenges gives you another reason to return. Once new equipment becomes available across your roster, it opens up further possibilities for future runs.

items.title: Warhammer Survivors is out now - review
items.summary: Warhammer Survivors has arrived from Auroch Digital as a licensed version of Vampire Survivors wearing the skin of Warhammer.
items.content:
Warhammer Survivors has arrived from Auroch Digital as a licensed version of Vampire Survivors wearing the skin of Warhammer. Note: this was a personal purchase.

Don't know what a bullet heaven is? You pick a character, run around with auto-attacks and pick up experience orbs (in this case, skulls) to level up. When you level up, you pick a new character buff or new / upgraded weapon to eventually become a bit over-powered. Eventually, the screen gets almost entirely filled with enemies and your weapons firing. Death is not the end, just another beginning as you unlock more of the game in terms of characters and items to find on your next run. Along with meta-progression, using earned coins during a run to continue to buff all characters permanently.

For anyone who has played the original Vampire Survivors - this is like seeing an old friend that now has a big bushy beard and an extra scar on their face. It's the same old but slightly different. You should be good to play this on basically anything, as it runs perfectly on desktop with Proton 11 and it's Steam Deck and Steam Machine Verified too.

I like how the game is split into two parts, giving you the different worlds of Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar. Each with their own characters and their own meta-progression. Here you get various characters and enemies from each universe, including Malum Caedo from Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun. It feels like the pacing on it is a good bit slower than VS and more zoomed-in. The main real difference here is the ability to build up a little squad. But, they didn't really do much with that idea. They're just faces for your guns, or swords - whatever. They stick with you, shoot and follow you around but that's it.

Quite punishing actually, especially early on when you've not done much of the meta progression. Enemies feel like a real bullet sponge - and the upgrades don't feel all that impactful a lot of the time. Then you unlock the third character in the 40K campaign, power up their main weapon and suddenly it's blissfully easy. The balancing is wildly off in Warhammer Survivors across many characters and the weapons. The campaigns too, Sigmar feels weirdly so much easier than 40K. I do like the exploding rolling dice though, that's a fun nod to the physical game. Same with the little paint pots to get more characters.

The pathfinding system is still the same from VS as well, enemies are dumb as rocks and walk into everything and like to get stuck quite often.

One design decision did really bug me with the Tyranids, loads of them have guns, but they don't fire at you. Why even give them guns in their design? Could have just given them anything else, since all they do is walk at you. That said, the artwork on all the enemies is great, the pixel artists did a wonderful job there.

YouTube will connect and may use cookies when you accept.

Overall - it's okay. It's not bad at all but it's not particularly exciting either. As a first entry into the genre for Warhammer fans, it will do just fine but it's not enough if you've played various other (and many much better) bullet heaven survivor-likes. It offers nothing really new to make it properly worth a visit. It's missing some special sauce that made the original Vampire Survivors so good.

Really, it's an overgrown DLC for Vampire Survivors that was released standalone.

I would have preferred it left in the oven to cook for a while longer, to bring some more new bits to the table, to really lean into the Warhammer world some more. Shame really, could have easily been a lot better. But that's just my opinion on it. It's okay if you feel differently, that's what makes us human.

Warhammer Survivors costs £6.39 / $7.99 / €7.49.

items.title: Warhammer Survivors Out Now on XBOX Game Pass! Defeat the Gloomspite Gitz With These Tips
items.summary: Warhammer Survivors is out now on XBOX Series X|S and XBOX Game Pass! Take a closer look at the Gloomsite Gitz enemy faction.
items.content:
If this is your first time hearing about Warhammer Survivors , buckle in for addictive bullet-heaven survivor gameplay set across the battlefields of the 41st Millennium and the Mortal Realms. You might know us, Auroch Digital, from our other Warhammer game, Warhammer 40,000 Boltgun . We’ve teamed up with poncle and Warhammer to create an officially licensed Warhammer Survivors .

Following the green theme of our previous entry , we’ve prepared a primer for you to take on the fungus-festooned Gloomspite Gitz!

The Gloomspite Gitz are a rabble of different cave-dwelling grots that worship the ‘Bad Moon’, a deity they believe will bring about the Everdank, an era of perpetual twilight. This calamitous cohort of crazed Gitz includes several enemy types, each with their own unique attacks and movement patterns you’ll need to learn to have any chance of survival!

Moonclan Stabbas are the foot soldiers of the Gloomspite Gitz, swarming the battlefield in tremendous numbers, stabbing wildly at everything in their path. Moonclan Stabbas try to overwhelm with sheer number of bodies and sharp, pointy objects – and while they may not be the scariest, look out for the company they keep…

…And the stampeding forces of the Squigalanche!

Squig Hoppers are grots that have bravely decided to mount feral Squigs and have somehow survived the process. These enemies bounce across the battlefield in unpredictable movements due to the nature of their wild mounts, and their attack damage will be bolstered by any nearby Loonboss on Giant Cave Squig who – you guessed it – also moves unpredictably!

Boinggrot Bounders , on the other hand, are veteran Squig-riders who have survived at least one battle (the life expectancy of a grot is low). For their prowess, they’ve been rewarded with lances, charging with precision toward the player.

Stampeding at the head of this Squigalanche are the wild and gargantuan Mangler Squigs. These two boisterous balls of fury are so ravenous they’ve been chained together. The beasts rampage across the screen, pulled taut by the chain that binds them together. Watch out for both the teeth of Mangler Squig and the chain as each can damage the player. Mangler Squigs always come in pairs, but when one dies, the remaining giant Squig becomes frenzied – deadlier than ever before!

If you can survive the pointy blades of the Gitz and the sharp teeth of the Squigs, then you may encounter an even greater threat… Troggoths!

Rockgut Troggoths lumber toward the player, and while they may be slow, they’re tough and have regeneration properties, making them tricky to bring down. Our recommendation? Get yourself a pair of Maleneth’s Poisoned Daggers and whittle them down from afar.

Should you survive all that, then we’ve got news for you: it doesn’t get better!

Trugg the Troggoth King is the mightiest of all troggoths, a towering mass of strength with an ill temper. He carries an arcane keystone of ancient design on his back which unleashes unpredictable bursts of elemental magic…

If you somehow manage to be strong enough to face this foe, he’ll begin the fight by swiping at you with his humungous Ironshell Club, which creates wide, telegraphed impact zones. If you’re hit, you’ll be sent flying. Trugg. You’ll also have to contend with that keystone of his, avoiding wild barrages of elemental projectiles. Getting hit by one of these stray projectiles will inflict your Survivor with negative status effects such as burning, poisoning, or bleeding.

As an Extremis-level threat, not just anyone, or any weapon, will be able to take down the Troggoth King. You’ll have to discover what his weakness is or face certain death!

items.title: Xbox Game Pass's free Vampire Survivors alternative stole 20 hours of my life in two days
items.summary: Vampire Survivors players have an excellent alternative to play now!
items.content:
I had to tap into the indomitable human spirit whilst playing Warhammer Survivors, as it's as brutal as the universe it's based on.

Last week I had some much-needed time off, and what better way to spend it than with early-access to one of my most-anticipated games of the year. I’ve developed a love-hate relationship with it though.

After the colossal success of Vampire Survivors loads of developers have tried to capitalise off the auto-battler’s success, but few have come close to the OG.

Warhammer Survivors is a different story however. It’s just as good, and I’m not just saying that because I’m a Warhammer fan.

Once installed, my intention was to play for around an hour before sorting out some errands around the house. Five hours later I was still playing.

You’re given the choice between two popular Warhammer settings. The first is Warhammer: Age of Sigmar, which is ideal for fantasy fans, but not really my cup of tea.

My bread and butter is Warhammer 40,000, and experiencing that universe in Vampire Survivors-style was more moreish than I’d ever expected.

The first round starred Ultramarine Malum Caedo, a popular character from the Warhammer 40,000 Boltgun games.

READ NEXT: Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2's grimdark goodness is so moreish I'll gladly give Games Workshop more money

A few scrappy Tyranids quickly fell to my chainsaw, with their numbers slowly growing like the satisfaction I felt cleaving through them.

Each level-up grants you a new ability, weapon, or upgrade and I’ve had so much fun unlocking them. I’ve still got plenty left as well, as most are locked behind secret characters.

However it hasn't all been sunshine and rainbows. The reason this game has devoured so much of my free time isn’t just because it’s fun, because it is, it’s also because it infuriates me unlike any other game I’ve played this year.

There’s nothing inherently hard about Warhammer Survivor s. All you do is move around, pick-up upgrades, and try to ensure our attacks are going into the bulk of the enemy’s forces to thin them down.

Like an actual game of Warhammer 40,000 though, luck is a huge factor. At the drop of a hat or the roll of a dice the game can be over in seconds as you didn’t manage to collect the upgrades needed for your build.

items.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl Meets Vampire Survivors In 9/10 100-Hour Free RPG
items.summary: This free RPG has 100+ hours of content.
items.content:
Art from Realm of the Mad God showcasing various enemies. Add ScreenRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Tom Wilson Published Nov 8, 2026, 12:00 AM EST Tom Wilson is a Gaming Features Writer at Screen Rant. Over the past five years, Tom has worked as the Editor-in-Chief at The Game Crater, as a Staff Writer for GamingIntel, a List Writer at TheGamer, and, of course, as a Senior Writer at ScreenRant. Tom has experience writing reviews, guides, news, and features, and has been responsible for teams of writers, training them and editing their work. Tom graduated with a Masters in Multimedia Journalism, and has since gone on to build up his portfolio of games journalism work. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap The sheer number of games like Vampire Survivors releasing today is utterly staggering. Its overwhelming visuals, endless barrage of upgrades, and deceptively complex gameplay are understandably enticing, further bolstered by the low price point and spec requirements. It is no wonder that Vampire Survivors and its abundance of pretenders have garnered such critical and commercial acclaim, especially in an era dominated by elevator-pitch concepts and a desire to move away from the relentless onslaught of live service fluff.

If the leagues of other games like Vampire Survivors have not yet proved sufficient, then there is another title worth trying. This massive, 100+ hour RPG takes a lot of the very best aspects of Vampire Survivors , sprinkles a healthy dash of Dungeon Crawler Carl -esque elements, and adds a core multiplayer component to craft a compelling experience that you can play completely for free. The best part is that it's a relatively old title, meaning it's had years of updates, improvements, and new features, all of which are available for you to enjoy right now.

The player fighting a boss in Realm of the Mad God. With even Warhammer getting a Survivors -like game , it feels as if every demographic has been catered to. This includes, of course, the Dungeon Crawler Carl fans, those looking for an experience closer to an RPG, or at least one involving dungeon delving and deadly boss battles. Fortunately, the long-running MMO (which predates the wonderful Vampire Survivors ), Realm of the Mad God , fits this bill perfectly, offering a chaotic, visually overwhelming, dungeon-based, RPG experience with bullet hell, Survivors -esque gameplay.

Released back in 2012, Realm of the Mad God has proven to be one of the most compelling MMOs on the market; its simplistic visuals and compelling core premise, alongside its huge focus on co-operative play and community, have helped keep its player counts consistently high, as has the steady stream of meaningful updates. Easily ranking among the greatest MMOs ever made , Realm of the Mad God , much like Vampire Survivors , understands how to hook the player and keep them coming back.

Its combination of a roguelike and MMO makes for an utterly unique experience unlike any other. It features permadeath, but it doesn't feel as punishing as one would expect from an MMO; the abundance of loot is ever tantalizing, as are the numerous classes you can choose from, the focus on group activities, and every high-stakes encounter that sees the screen awash with pixelated projectiles cascading wildly. Ostensibly, Realm of the Mad God dared to dream of an MMO Vampire Survivors over a decade before it came out.

The player in a shop in Realm of the Mad God. Being an MMO that has been around for nearly 15 years, Realm of the Mad God features hundreds of hours of content for players to get stuck into. You can also play it for free fairly reliably; its vast array of microtransactions typically skews toward the realm of cosmetics and convenience. Of course, that doesn't mean you won't encounter some level of grind or frustration, but you're bound to get a rather substantial amount of Vampire Survivors -esque fun out of it long before you hit that point.

Realm of the Mad God is currently only available on PC. You can download it via its official Steam store page .

One has to enjoy MMOs, however, in order to truly get the most out of Realm of the Mad God . While it is certainly playable solo, engaging with its guilds or playing with friends is ultimately the main way of enjoying it. Should you engage with its community and co-operative gameplay, you'll have a great time and find yourself with dozens, if not hundreds, of hours of fun. If you've been looking for a Vampire Survivors -like with a dash of Dungeon Crawler Carl sprinkled in, then you should absolutely give Realm of the Mad God a try.

items.title: Bullet Heaven Games: auto-shooters, reverse bullet hells, and games like Vampire Survivors
items.summary: Games like Vampire Survivors, including: Picayune Dreams, Brotato, Deep Rock Galactic: Survivors, Soulstone Survivors, and The Spell Brigade.
items.content:
Welcome, Dear Reader, to Rogueliker’s guide to the best bullet heaven games, reverse bullet hells, auto-shooters, and survivors-likes – that is, these are the best games like Vampire Survivors.

Which brings us neatly to our starting point: Vampire Survivors, a game that has become something of a cultural phenomenon. The game had a growing audience even before Phil Spencer (the man in charge of Xbox) revealed that he had been playing it obsessively. Spencer’s public confession, however, put the game on millions of radars, and Poncle’s auto-shooter hasn’t looked back since.

Not only has Vampire Survivors continued to enjoy success, but it has also inspired a tidal wave of reverent auto-shooters, cheeky clones, and clever copycats. Simply put: if you like Poncle’s so-called bullet heaven game, you are currently being well served with new offerings.

Because this burgeoning sub-genre of gaming continues to grow, and considering the fact that I’ve played both Vampire Survivors and a decent number of similarly structured action-roguelites, I figured it was time to put together a feature that highlighted a number of auto-shooters. Now, anyone who is eager for more can easily get started on something new.

Before that, if you’d like a deeper dive into the finest games that the wider genre has to offer, check out our guide to the best roguelikes, roguelites, and roguelike-likes.

This one gets a section all to itself. I mean, it’s the reason that we’re all here, isn’t it? Vampire Survivors is a very personal recommendation from me; I played the game A LOT after discovering it. In fact, it was the game I played after completing Hades, and after spending hundreds of hours with both, and after seeing how popular these games were, I figured that making Rogueliker was worth a shot.

I’ve been a big fan of roguelikes, roguelites, and I think also games with permadeath and deep, interlocking systems for a while. Vampire Survivors delivers so much on that final front, chiefly via its wealth of playable characters, each one tuned slightly differently and with their own starting weapons. There are also loads of levels to unlock and explore, and each one is riddled with secrets to discover.

What I love the most about Vampire Survivors is the way the game feels to play. After intense speed runs with Zagreus in Hades, it was nice to just stroll around whacking things with a whip/sword/bird strike and making an interesting decision every few minutes. The game’s one-stick controls are so intuitive and the gameplay so straightforward, it’s so easy to fall for its considerable charms.

Once that happens to you, you’re done for because there’s so much game here just waiting for you to explore. What’s more, it’s a generous game with a low starting cost and reasonably priced DLC expansions. Speaking of expansions, I mentioned that the game was a “cultural phenomenon” up top, and that wasn’t hyperbole, as Vampire Survivors’ expansions include Among Us and Contra, plus the game itself has been appearing in other places, including a favourite game of mine, Balatro .

If you’re done with Vampire Survivors but want more of that sweet reverse bullet hell gameplay, your next port of call might well be Picayune Dreams.

This bold, surreal space shooter is undoubtedly inspired by Vampire Survivors, but to the credit of the game’s designers, they’ve kept a similar spirit but expressed it very differently. For starters, you can take control of the action more directly with the auto-shooter element being a toggleable option, and that makes a difference.

Enemies drop numbers when they perish, and bigger numbers will help you level more quickly. There’s transmogrification, which means you can see the items as they’re added to your avatar. Enemy designs are surreal, and the whole thing feels much more thematically independent than most other auto-shooters. The story is enigmatic and full of mystery. Finally, there are boss battles where the action descends into bullet hell; a crowning twist that makes Picayune Dreams one of the best games in the genre.

My third highlight is Brotato, a game that offers a similar-yet-very-different experience from the above top picks. This is a very silly game that doesn’t take itself too seriously, yet it also delivers a fun and constantly rewarding experience.

The key differentiator here is the tightly controlled arenas. Vampire Survivors has vast, sprawling levels, and Picayune Dreams has you floating around in the vastness of space, but Brotato keeps the action on a much tighter leash; you can only roam around a small square here. Instead of exploration, the focus is more on staying nimble and moving quickly and, of course, taking down your enemies.

items.title: Warhammer Survivors is more than just a Vampire Survivors spin-off
items.summary: Even as we drown in Warhammer games, Survivors stands out as something extremely cool.
items.content:
Roguelike Warhammer Survivors is more than just a Vampire Survivors spin-off Features By Fraser Brown Published 6 October 2026 Even as we drown in Warhammer games, Survivors stands out as something extremely cool.

a]:text-inherit [&>a]:underline"> When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Auroch Digital) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter I thought Warhammer Survivors sounded like a neat spin-off—Vampire Survivors in a Warhammer skin, created by Boltgun developer Auroch Digital. Having spent 10 hours with its demo, however, I'm increasingly convinced that it deserves to be catagorised as a sequel.

A lot of care has clearly gone into the hero design, maps and all the horrible beasties trying to eviscerate you, and rather than simply replicate Vampire Survivors, Auroch Digital has included a bunch of novelties and new ideas, like followers and more overt boss battles.

Playing it on my Steam Deck has already had a terrible impact on my sleep routine, just like its predecessor. And with its launch just around the corner on November 10, I think I'm just going to have to accept that I'm going to be very tired for the rest of the year.

Weapon evolutions, enemies that drop chests with multiple items, arcana, bosses, challenges, upgrades—if it's in Vampire Survivors, it's probably in Warhammer Survivors, albeit with some Warhammer-themed twists. Instead of experience gems, for instance, you get experience skulls (because of course you do). And instead of Red Death, you get Extremis bosses, massive seemingly invincible bastards—until you figure out the trick to destroying them.

I have used buckets of Nuln oil in my Warhammer painting endeavours—and yes, I've spilled a lot of it. On my jeans, on my carpet, one time on my dog. But it's never hurt anyone. In Warhammer Survivors, it's been weaponised, damaging and slowing ememies, as well as making them more flammable. You'll also be able to get your hands on explosive dice, which roll across the battlefield before going kaboom! I'm sure there are rules against this.

The first WH40k map sees you running around a battlefield that's being swallowed up by tyranids. It's aggressively pink and full of horrible pustules and grotesque alien topography. In Age of Sigmar, meanwhile, it's skaven time! Nasty little rodents, glowing warpstones, you know the deal. There's even a map that's just your tabletop, full of paints and measuring tape, where all the game's monstrosities gather together to take you out.

While Warhammer Survivors is a singleplayer romp, that doesn't mean you're all alone. Unlockable characters can be rescued once you defeat the enemies harassing them, after which they'll join you in battle. In subsequent fights, they'll rejoin you when you select one of their associated weapons when you level up. At least one character gets buffs from having more followers, and upgrading his lasgun also lets him run around with his fellow Astra Militarum grunts.

I've poured hundreds of hours into Vampire Survivors, and Warhammer Survivors might be a bit trickier. Battles escalate a lot faster, and it took me longer to figure out good weapon combos that worked to thin the herd. I was a lot more desperate for healing than I'm used to with its predecessor. I think I'd prefer the early game to be slightly less intense, though the issue might be that the demo features fewer weapons and characters, which could be making it feel a touch more challenging than it actually is.

Enemy factions benefit from unique traits that may give you a bit of a hard time. Tyranids, for instance, can be empowered by more intelligent members of their species, which use their synapse power to enrage lesser critters within their radius. So you'll want to take these psychic beasties down quickly. Orks, meanwhile, can get all riled up, kicking off a WAAAGH, where they spawn in greater numbers and become faster and stronger.

When you play Warhammer Survivors, you select a universe first. Characters, upgrades and unlocks are specific to each universe, though you will find some passive abilities repeated in both. It feels like two spin-offs collected in a single game.

Vampire Survivors is the game that really justified my purchase of a Steam Deck, and while developer Auroch Digital still says it's working on compatibility, it already feels great on my Deck. It's where I've spent most of my time playing it and I've got no complaints.

Cancel all of your plans in November, because Warhammer Survivors is launching on the 10th. And I've got high hopes for it. Yes, it's a spin-off, but it also feels like a proper Vampire Survivors sequel and potentially my favourite bullet heaven since the OG.

items.title: How Vampire Survivors became Vampire Crawlers: Six lessons from building a game based on another developer's IP
items.summary: Nosebleed Interactive's Andreas Firnigl on crafting a spin-off of Poncle's smash hit: pub prototypes, shared rules, last-minute changes and more
items.content:
Nosebleed Interactive's Andreas Firnigl on crafting a spin-off of Poncle's smash hit: pub prototypes, shared rules, last-minute changes and more

Image credit: Nosebleed Interactive/Poncle Academy by Andreas Firnigl CEO, Nosebleed Interactive Published on Aug. 10, 2026, 3:19 p.m. Follow Nosebleed Interactive Andreas Firnigl started his career as a tester on Big Mutha Truckers, way back on Gamecube. He founded Nosebleed Interactive almost 15 years ago as CEO and creative director.

In 2023, an old contact I had worked with 15 years ago – and who is now at Poncle – came to us with the amazing opportunity to collaborate on a Vampire Survivors spin-off.

Luca Galante, the creator of Vampire Survivors, had come up with the idea for a card game spin-off and had already developed an early prototype, but Poncle wanted an external studio to help turn it into a complete game. So lead designer Luke Wintflint and I worked with Luca and Poncle to evolve that idea into what became Vampire Crawlers.

After 15 years making games and working with other studios, Nosebleed Interactive has learnt a lot about how to treat someone else's IP and how to collaborate with external partners. We learnt even more on Crawlers, and I want to share some key lessons that you can take away and apply at your own studio.

Naturally, understanding the IP you are working on is vital. Yet it's even more important to demonstrate to the client that you understand it.

I've put a stupid amount of hours into Vampire Survivors in order to understand all the little nuances and tics that most people won't notice. This kind of intense playing helps you to understand what is changeable and what is not. Some things will be fundamental to the experience and will have to be incorporated, while others are things that, frankly, players don't care about all that much. Knowing what can and can't be changed is a sign you are working on something you understand, rather than doing a half-arsed superficial imitation.

The fundamentals of Vampire Crawlers came together very quickly. A pen and paper version that we played in the pub during the early days of development was surprisingly close to the final game. However, in those early months, we paid less attention to the IP and were instead focused on adding content, throwing in random stuff willy-nilly as a placeholder. We knew it would be quick and easy to fix later on, and knew enough about the IP to do it right – but Poncle didn't.

We had the bones of a great game, but it wasn't clear to Poncle that we had a good Vampire Survivors game. So we downed tools on everything else and focused on fixing that – making sure all the names were right, matching up how stats would transfer from Survivors to Crawlers, and so on. As soon as Poncle saw the next build, they gave us the green light.

In short, do that work of understanding your partner's IP – but make sure you show them you have that understanding, too.

Fans of the IP will naturally be interested in playing your new game, but you also need to make sure it works for people who don't know the original title. This is why it's important to get feedback from people who haven't played the IP at all.

There were a couple of people at Nosebleed who hadn't played Vampire Survivors, and rather than encouraging them to try the game, we asked them to avoid playing it at all. Having some folks on the team who are coming in clean, as it were, was a real help to balance the onboarding, which is so important in this kind of game. Relying too much on knowledge of the existing IP could make it less attractive to new players.

Your partner is working with you because you have something to bring to the table (there's certainly a lot of Nosebleed's DNA in Vampire Crawlers). So lean into your strengths – but be humble. Be prepared to learn from how your partner works, and what works for their IP.

Before Crawlers, we'd just come off Arcade Paradise, where the density of every pixel had to be exactly correct. Would Poncle do that? No.

🟣 Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton

A few days back we announced Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton in collaboration with Shueisha Games! Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton is a game like Vampire Survivors, but with a twist: you'll be able to play an 8-player survivors royale PvPvE mode! Some in-game names and terminology are still in development and may be subject to change. While every player plays in their own world, you accumulate points by defeating curses and sorcerers, and with every 100 points accumulated you get to choose a Rule Change that can affect everyone's game. Some Rule Changes are INSANE, but for now we'll just reveal the simple ones you can see in the trailer (silence, slow, steal points...). But Rule Changes aren't the only way to interact with other players. Introducing a world first, mind blowing, unbelievable game mechanic: PRESS A BUTTON. While you move your auto-attacking character, your special attack also builds up. By PRESSING A BUTTON when the special attack is ready, you get to unleash your character's Special Attack, or, if that character can, a DOMAIN EXPANSION! Other players can be caught in the effect of your Domain or Special Attack, so you have to keep an eye on other players' position and special-bar status. A very important aspect of the 8-players mode is the Live Match Status Feed (working name). This big chunk of UI on the left side of the screen constantly updates in real time, acting not only as a scoreboard, but also sending out warnings and all kind of information about what the other players are up to. At the end of the 15 minutes battle royale, the 2 players with the most points will face one another in a 19 seconds duel. Despite the online focus, Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton is a game you can also play alone, in a mission-based mode, just like Vampire Survivors. If you don't ever want to go online, you'll still be able to play the 8-players battle royale mode against bots. This is a game you buy once and can play anytime. We'll keep supporting the game after launch, with our usual style of content updates. So forget about gatcha elements or a forever-evolving PvP meta keeping your time and wallet hostages: our focus here are fun and affordability. Apologies if you had enough of this wall of text, but I kepty mouth shut for almost two years and I haven't even got to the technical bits yet! Yes, the game runs on the Vampire Survivors - First Survivaton framework, so you can expect that same familiar experience playing it, but we had to do several unique tweaks for Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble Survivaton. Other than the obvious, completely new networking for the gameplay and Live Match Status Feed, we have doubled the resolution at which the game runs. That allowed us to completely rebuild the whole VFX pipeline so that we could re-create the distinctive look of Curse Energy and the changes the whole stage depending on activated Domain Expansions or Special Attacks. Another reason to double the resolution was to properly display the UI (that has been completely reworked at framework level) and the Live Match Status Feed, that is capable of also streaming gameplay snippets from other online players. You'll see a lot of other tweaks, like the fact that characters look different if they are seen from the left or from the right, a "default attack" per character that triggers without any weapon, or walls that are actually solid to name a few. Then there are other changes that won't be noticeable until you get to play the game. For example, while we are going by the same content-unlock-philosophy as Vampire Survivors, we are completely reworking the progression in the various game modes and also per-character, so that every game mode will feel fresh even to VS veterans. That's all for now, I hope you have enjoyed the trailer; my favourite part was that bit were Gojo takes a walk.

🔴 Bloodmoon character tease

Legacy of the Bloodmoon is almost complete and we will be able to start testing and submissions soon! That means we'll have an actual release date soon too. In the meantime, here's a Character Spotlight video about Malice Bloodmoon:

🔴 ARG and Community Character Competition winners

Congratulations to the trio of winners of the Lucca Comics ARG: Jenoss, Miryel, Siming, and GIU_LLS (:poemg:?), and to DissonantSynth for winning the Community Challenge! We're finally getting into the design stage of the characters, with a first implementation that will soon be shared with the winners, behind the scenes, to start iterating together on gameplay mechanics. You can expect a few surprises and little extras about them when they'll make their appearance in the game! Baron Husker and Sefi Rotto (:poemg:?) will come alive in a later update, v1.17

🔴 First steps for Steam Workshop support

Instead of waiting the conclusion of the current cycles of updates for Vampire Survivors as originally planned, we will develop modding support over time, one feature at a time. Feature 1 will be about adding CUSTOM (private/local) and WORKSHOP (public/Steam Workshop) characters! Please join the Discord or use the public-beta forum if you're interested in trying out custom characters before they go live on the main branch, in a future update (currently aiming for v1.17)

🔴 Vampire Survivors Comics

Vampire Survivor is getting comics! We've been working with Titan Comics on a 4-issue series, written by David Hazan and illustrated by Jimm Kucaj, with the first issue coming out this September, available in 3 cover variants. Some familiar Vampire Survivors will go through Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, and a few other places, and there might even be some lore in there. Issue #1 is available to pre-order from your local comic shop or from Forbidden Planet if you're in the UK / EU. You can find out more about the comics on the Titan Comics website.

🔵 Vampire Crawlers: first QOL update

Our first update to Vampire Crawlers add an Endless mode and several QOL improvements! You can find more details, the strategy behind future updates, and some content spoilers in the Steam News here.

🟢 Countup to the next announcement

Look, we're doing a lot of stuff across several small teams. I'm always happy to write the Steam News but I cannot bombard your feed with everything we're doing. Also took me something like 3 weeks to set this all up. So if you'd like to hear about what we're doing a bit more often, then please visit poncleup.com to see a recap or subscribe to our newsletter. It's a countup instead of a countdown because, as you might have noticed, we're release-date-averse and have no idea ourselves when we'll drop something new 🤷‍♂️ Just know that the newsletters are written by the marketing team :vsskull: Alright, I'm done with work, time to go back having fun on my secret project. Thank you everyone, I'll leave you in the self-proclaimed capable hands of the marketing team! - Luca

  • 2 New Characters
  • either 2 or 10 new weapons 🤷‍♂️
  • 3 New Darkanas
  • 1 New Music Track
  • 3 new Relics, of which 1 Secret rather than Unlockable

Other tweaks and features

  • "Random LevelUp" can now be toggled during a run if it is already unlocked on the Stage menu
  • Added option to Unbanish a weapon when picking it up from the stage
  • Buffed a few weapons like Magi-Stone and Mille Bolle Blu
  • Rendering fixes for a few weapons, including birds, Prismatic Missile, Runetracer…
Patch 1.15 will be released on all other platforms a bit later, by the end of the month, due to platform-specific optimizations and differences in save slots management. On the bright side, we will also be releasing a Nintendo Switch 2 version, with better performance and mouse support!

Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is coming Summer 2026

https://store.steampowered.com/app/4781330/Vampire_Survivors_Legacy_of_the_Bloodmoon/ Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is our “accidental” next expansion and the evil twin to Legacy of the Moonspell. The original plan was just to make a little content update to Legacy of the Moonspell. Since it’s the first and smallest VS expansion, it felt right to try to balance its value a little. Needless to say, ideas started to flow and everything spiraled into a much bigger project. I’m not sure I’ll ever learn at this stage. In the end, Legacy of the Moonspell will be getting its content buff (7 new unlocks) and Legacy of the Bloodmoon will live a life of its own. This expansion pack follows Clan Bloodmoon as they retrace the pilgrimage of Saint Baal’Thasar, in search of a paradise lit by (you guessed it) a bright red moon. There is also an ancient manor that may or may not hide the secret of immortality. Legacy of the Bloodmoon will contain:
  • 12 new villains friendly characters
  • 16+ new weapons and evolutions, including a FireBall
  • 8 savage new music tracks
  • 1 new adventure
  • 1 new very large stage
  • Interesting bits and bobs I won’t spoil at this time
But there’s more. Legacy of the Bloodmoon will cost approximately 1 money (0.99 USD), and Legacy of the Moonspell will receive a price cut and also be priced 1 money :) You can find all details about Legacy of the Bloodmoon below, now here’s a villainous trailer about it:

Vampire Survivors - First Survivaton

Among the many projects we’re working on (approximately 15 projects, not 15 games, please don’t panic) there is also a lineup of Survivaton games. It’s definitely a meaningful word that means “survive a ton” and nothing else. These are games like Vampire Survivors, developed internally at poncle, tied to IPs that might need unique game mechanics, a different graphic style, or are so expansive that ultimately deserve their own standalone game (compared to making a DLC for VS). I’d love to make examples, but I’d have to spoil way too much. Being developed internally, we’ll be able to guarantee affordability and worthwhile titles. Since a good 90% of global VS players aren’t reached by the Steam news (or are not interested in gaming news in general), the best way to also let them know that the Survivatons are tied directly to VS is to also call VS a Survivaton, hence the new sub-title. Please note there’s a dash before First Survivaton instead of a semi-colon, because DLCs exist... The next time I name a game I’ll remember to not use something as generic as “Monster Hunter” as inspiration please know I love Monster Hunter 💌

poncle Japan

We can finally say we are building poncle Japan! It will be poncle, but in Japan. The new studio is headed by Sawaki Takeyasu, known for his work on Devil May Cry, Ōkami, and El Shaddai: Ascension of the Metatron. Having a studio in Japan will simplify and speed up the work we do with all our Japanese partners, and also bring new opportunities for collabs. It’s too soon to say what the team will be working on; we are planning to fully open the studio by the end of 2026. Now it's time for all the FAQs and info blocks, thanks for reading and waiting patiently for this update! - Luca

Legacy of the Bloodmoon FAQs

When does it release? Summer 2026. What do you define as summer? Not winter. How much does it cost? Around £0.95, with regional pricing varying by platform and country. Why will Legacy of the Moonspell’s price change too? It felt right to adjust the price so that it’s more balanced compared to the amount of content of the other expansions. Please note that some stores have minimum prices in certain countries. In some places, Moonspell was already too cheap to make it cheaper. What about Tides of the Foscari then? Please at least wait for Moonspell and Bloodmoon before asking for more, we know we know 😭 Will Moonspell get new content too? Yes, 7 new unlocks for a few more weapons and characters. Is Vampire Survivors still getting free updates? Yes of course, there’s still plenty on the roadmap.

Update 1.15 Full spoilers

♫ Murder on the Seafloor Composed and arranged by Filippo Vicarelli.

Quick content guide:

  • Collect a total of 50 Vacuums to unlock The Lycaeum stage
  • Find the Penshin Fatcha in The Lycaeum and see all its evolutions to unlock it permanently
  • Survive 20 minutes in The Lycaeum to unlock Para Kooleo
  • Trigger a Lavatrix Machina with Para Kooleo to unlock Darkana VIII - Edge of the Earth
  • Buy the Survarocchi at the top of The Lycaeum to unlock them for any character
  • Buy the Green Eyes Vizard at the top of The Lycaeum to be able to find Bat Dragons in other stages
  • Defeat any Bat Dragon (Currently available in Mad Forest and Il Molise) to unlock the Unearthly Bolt wea;on
  • Evolve the Unearthly Bolt with a maxed Tirajisú to unlock Big Troubler
  • Defeat any Bat Dragon with Big Troubler and Arcana 0 - Game Killer to unlock Darkana 0 - Stake to your Heart
  • Survive 15 minutes in Inverse Boss Rash with Random Events and Random Level Ups to unlock Darkana XIX - Heir of Fate
  • Defeat 2 unique Bat Dragons to unlock a new set of Survarots to purchase from Big Troubler

Detailed info

New stage: The Lycaeum An underwater-themed stage where you press some buttons, beat some crabs, run to the center, kill more things, press more buttons, don’t die. The Drowner can only be defeated via raw damage or by reaching the top of the stage. Hidden treasures can be collected only using Mad Groove or Lavatrix Machina. Teleporters become active after reaching the top once. New character: Para Kooleo Starts with a Move Speed and Duration bonus. When his HP drops below a certain threshold it triggers a Vacuum. He also likes to evolve weapons. He has an abundance of skins. New character: Big Troubler Loves gold and gets trigger happy when he gets gold. The gold also loves him and will protect him at all costs. New weapon: Penshin Fatcha & Tonno Subito / Tonnado / Tonn’omoto / Tonn’oddeeo / Tonne / Unsurpassed / Miracle of Multiplication. Starting weapon for Para Kooleo. Select one of six tuna forms. Evolve it from one to another, stacking stats as you go. Evolve at least once to transform all the Vacuums pickup into "Lavatrix Machina". Then, if you choose to, evolve into the secret evolution, Miracle of Multiplication where everything happens at once. Does not require any items to evolve, but many, many treasure chests. New weapon: Unearthly Bolt & Spirit Disturbance Starting weapon of Big Troubler. Spawns green bolts that attack the closest enemy. It deals increasingly high damage if it Crits in rapid succession. The cap for this damage bonus is determined by Revivals. Evolve with a maxed out Tirajisú. The evolution spawns a green dragon that always deals critical hits. New relic: Green Eyes Vizard Bat Dragons will appear on the Stage Selection menu until they have been defeated at least once. They will appear on the map during a run, and they have to be activated by getting hit. Once active, time stops and enemy waves are changed until they are killed. You can fight them again in new runs, they simply won't be signaled in Stage Selection anymore after getting killed once. New Darkanas: 0 - Stake to your Heart Unlocked by defeating a Bat Dragon with Big Troubler while using the Game Killer Arcana. You will no longer be able to level up using experience gems. Instead, when defeating an enemy, they will also drop a Gold Coin, that you’ll be able to spend at a special merchant to buy weapons. Gold coins will also become your health: don't reach 0 (and quit before Red Death deals the usual 65535 damage per hit to you) New Darkanas: VIII - Edge of the Earth Unlocked by triggering a Lavatrix Machina with Para Kooleo. Gain Thorns and Move Speed locked at 200%, ignore walls, destroy light sources upon contact, and attract things that normally aren’t attracted by a Magnet, like treasure chests. New Darkanas: XIX - Heir of Fate Unlocked by surviving 15 minutes in inverse Boss Rash with Random Events and Random Level Ups enabled. While active, defeating enemies with Fire damage causes them to drop Scorched Souls. Additionally, a Nduja Fritta Tanto will trigger when the character's Health dips to a certain point. New Relics: Survarocchi Unlocked by purchasing it from the Big Troubler merchant in The Lycaeum. Allows Survarot cards to spawn from light sources. Previously available only via the Ante Chamber dlc and a secret character, Survarots Enemahs (Secret rather than Unlockable) Unlocked by purchasing it from the Big Troubler merchant in The Lycaeum after defeating any two unique Bat Dragons. Adds an extra 18 cards based on various enemies to drafts of Survarot. For the full list of bugfixes, please see here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1794680/view/693137145499484509

1.15 FAQs

How much is 1.15? It’s a free update. Can I now share DLCs when playing online? Not yet, in this patch we managed to do the groundwork to allow for DLC sharing, but we still have to complete the feature. Can I now use Cross-save on PS and Apple+? Not yet. We still don’t have the right policies in place to do that. What platforms is update 1.15 available on? Update 1.15 is launching on Steam first. Other platforms are planned to follow by the end of the month, including Xbox, PlayStation 4/5, Nintendo Switch, Android, iOS, and Epic Games Store. Is update 1.15 coming to Nintendo Switch 2? Yes! Update 1.15 will bring Vampire Survivors to Nintendo Switch 2 for the first time. It won’t arrive at the exact same time as the other platforms, but the current plan is for Nintendo Switch 2 support to follow around two weeks after update 1.15 (but don’t hold us to that). Where are the new achievements? We will sort out the new Steam achievements in the next patch (they will pop automatically). Hey are you still updating Vampire Crawlers? Yes of course, it’s taking longer than expected to release the first QOL improvements patch and a cute looking roadmap because we got stuck for days trying to exit the game.

Christopher Dring Apr 22 16 2 Share The Game Business is Live in Los Angeles on Monday, June 8, where we will be interviewing video game royalty Laura Miele, Jason Rubin and Matthew Ball live on stage. Tickets are available now.

Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube In This Edition, Poncle’s Matteo Sapio on: - Vampire Survivors spin-offs and tie-ins - Opening studios in Japan and Italy - Working on over 15 projects

During last week’s London Game Festival, I spoke with Matteo Sapio, the chief strategy officer at Vampires Survivors developer Poncle.

We were speaking in front of a live audience, and it was one of the most revealing interviews I’ve done since launching The Game Business . During out chat, Sapio announced:

That Vampire Survivors has now surpassed 27 million players

It has over 15 projects in active development (and even more in earlier stages)

It is licensing out its engine to other brands and studios to build ‘Survivors’ games based on popular IP

It has paused its third-party publishing plans

“Vampire Survivors came from a solo developer,” Sapio explains. “It was Luca Galante, who made a game for him and his friends. Vampire Survivors exploded, and in two or three months, it sold more than one million copies. Luca’s yachts are video games. So instead of buying a yacht, he made the Emerald Beyond DLC [for Vampire Survivors] with Square Enix, which we released for free. Things grew organically from there.”

For more surprising developer interviews, sign-up to The Game Business today

First, there are spin-offs to Vampire Survivors. This includes the deck-building card battler Vampire Crawlers, which is out this week.

“We [are using] the famous Vampire Survivors IP to experiment in new genres,” Sapio tells us. “We love card games, but we are not very good at card games. They’re complicated. So, we made the game that we wanted to play.”

Vampire Crawlers is out this week Second, Poncle is working on original IP. Sapio says the company is currently developing two entirely original properties.
